subsystems.name: Epidural paddle electrode array
subsystems.role: delivers current to the dorsal surface of the spinal cord over the segments that control the legs.

subsystems.name: Implanted pulse generator
subsystems.role: generates the timed pulse trains and stores the programs.

subsystems.name: Lead and extension
subsystems.role: carries current from the implanted generator to the paddle, with strain reliefs so it survives years of movement.

subsystems.name: External controller and programmer
subsystems.role: lets the user switch programs and the clinician map contacts and set dose.

subsystems.name: Sensing and timing layer
subsystems.role: decides when to stimulate — synchronised to residual voluntary intent or to measured muscle activity rather than running continuously.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the paddle
buildSteps.detail: Contacts are laser-cut or stamped from platinum–iridium, welded to conductors, then moulded into a thin silicone carrier that will lie flat against the dura.

buildSteps.title: Build the generator
buildSteps.detail: Circuit boards, battery and telemetry coil are sealed inside a titanium can, welded shut and helium leak-tested.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Lead, paddle and generator are joined, the connector is over-moulded, and feedthroughs are sealed so no body fluid reaches the electronics.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for a lifetime of bending
buildSteps.detail: Accelerated flexion and corrosion testing, plus sterilisation, is required because the device cannot easily be replaced.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: Through a laminotomy at a thoracic level below the injury, the surgeon slides the paddle into the dorsal epidural space under imaging guidance and tunnels the lead to a pocket in the lower back or abdomen.

buildSteps.title: Map and program
buildSteps.detail: Each contact is tested to find which evoke leg muscle responses with the least discomfort; amplitude, pulse width (hundreds of microseconds) and frequency (tens of hertz) are tuned to the individual.

buildSteps.title: Tune the timing
buildSteps.detail: Stimulation is made to arrive at the right moment — gated by attempted movement or by sensor feedback — so it reinforces a command rather than producing a rigid posture.

buildSteps.title: Train intensively
buildSteps.detail: Weeks of task-specific, body-weight-supported standing and stepping practice with the stimulator on teach the cord to use the incoming signal; the training is as important as the hardware.

prerequisites.why: decades of spinal-cord stimulators for pain established the electrodes, generators and surgical routines.
the mechanism relies on recruiting large sensory fibres that feed the cord's own walking circuitry; the details are still being mapped.
patients need imaging later, and an implanted array must not make that impossible or dangerous.
continuous stimulation helps, but matching it to the person's own movement intent is what makes walking fluid.
outcomes depend on long supervised training programmes, which are costly and not universally available.

pathway.milestone: single-centre and small multi-patient trials in chronic paralysis, with several patients standing, stepping and walking with support
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the cord's dormant circuitry can be re-engaged years after injury.

pathway.milestone: larger controlled trials and regulatory clearance for a defined indication
pathway.unlocks: reimbursed, commercially available therapy rather than experimental surgery.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop systems coupling the stimulator to cortical or muscle signals
pathway.unlocks: more natural timing and less fatigue.

pathway.milestone: home-use systems plus combination with regenerative or biological repair
pathway.unlocks: function that persists without constant stimulation.
